newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends up on institutional buying.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends up on institutional buying.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up on Wednesday on large amounts of buying from institutional investors, traders said.

The most actively traded November 1997 contract ended at 21,000 yuan ($2,533) per tonne, rising 300 yuan. It opened at 20,550 yuan, hitting an intraday low of 20,450 and a high of 21,030 yuan per tonne.
August rose 200 to 20,700 yuan, September 350 to 20,800, October 300 to 21,000, December 300 to 21,000, the January 1997 contract 270 to 21,000.
Combined volume fell to 74,080 tonnes from 91,280 tonnes.
Copper opened lower and moved at low levels in the morning session before large amounts of buying pushed prices up to near their intraday highs.
Traders said institutional buyers built large long positions on Wednesday despite overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange (LME).
"Institutional buying is responsible for today's gains and a strong rebound attracted much follow-up buying from retail investors," one trader said.
"But copper met strong resistance at the 21,000 yuan level today, indicating new incentives are needed," he added.
LME copper was expected to remain under pressure on Wednesday, analysts in London said, adding that prices could head towards support levels after a stocks rise of 5,000 tonnes.
In early trade, LME copper gyrated below $2,300 a tonne, which traders said was the next key resistance point.
In Shanghai, physical copper prices rose to 20,800-20,850 yuan from 20,600 due to the strong futures performance.
Traders said market sentiment continued to improved on Wednesday and the red metal was likely to rise further in the next few days.
"Copper will continue its upward trend in the short term if it can stand steady around the key 21,000 yuan level," a second trader said.
August rose 100 yuan to 13,850, September 190 to 14,090, October 440 to 14,120, November 400 to 14,050 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 3,730 tonnes from 2,840 tonnes.
